[[☃ image 1]]

Then we can draw a few random points, perform the transformation, and see what happens!

options.alt: A vertical line l. Point P is at the top to the right of the line. Point Q is on the left side of the line close to the bottom. Point A is directly on the line.

hints.content:
[[☃ image 1]]

Each point maps to the other side of $\ell$ and remains the same distance from $\ell$. Also, the segments between each pre-image and image are perpendicular to $\ell$. Therefore, this transformation is a reflection.

A prime is were A is located. Point P prime is on the opposite side of the line from point P with a congruent distance away. Point Q prime is on the opposite side of the line from point Q with a congruent distance away. A dashed circle passes through P and P prime forming the diameter of the circle. A dashed circle passes through Q and Q prime forming the diameter of the circle.

question.content:
A certain mapping in the $xy$-plane has the following properties:

- Every point $A$ on line $\ell$ maps to itself.
- Every point $P$ that isn't on $\ell$ maps to a point $P'$ such that $\overline{PP'}$ is the diameter of a circle centered on $\ell$, and $\overline{PP'}$ is perpendicular to $\ell$.

**Which transformation does the mapping define?**

[[☃ radio 1]]
